The STEEL team would like to add this to the agenda

* WELDing the STEEL: EELS + EEST merger, changes and updates
[Portmanteau wanted for Heka + Bogotá upgrade](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/portmanteau-for-heka-bogota-upgrade-after-glamsterdam/26400) after Glamsterdam

Light client perspective of Glamsterdam EIPs: https://pureth.guide/glamsterdam

A couple notes on some popular proposals, as I won't be on the call.

### [EIP-7708: ETH transfers emit a log](https://forkcast.org/upgrade/glamsterdam#eip-7708)

- Misses 0-value tx, fees (regular + priority), and withdrawal credits. Is it useful enough standalone for G*?
- Prio fees (separate recipient than regular fee!) means having hundreds of extra micro-payments per block. Prio fees also bad for scaling due to continuous write lock on fee recipient balance
- [EIP-7799](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7799) consolidates all prio payments, impacts mevboost builder as the prio fee can only be spent in the next block
- Parts could be:
    - (a) EIP-7708 + [0-value tx add-on](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9003/files), allow enumerating all tx where the wallet was involved in
    - (b) EIP-7799 for fees + withdrawals. Note this changes block header (maybe better in H*)

### [EIP-7745: Trustless log index](https://forkcast.org/upgrade/glamsterdam/#eip-7745)
     
- The EIP is super important, but rushing for a June release is too early.
- Very tricky to implement correctly, involves database, reorg handling, and complex data structure.
- Proof format still in progress, network sync protocol missing, non-standard SSZ usage (list with different element types, holes in list, 6466 Log container and 7916 ProgressiveList need bumps to latest specs)
- Parts could be:
    - (a) Implement any accelerated eth_getLogs index in ELs. Does not need coordination
    - (b) Finish the proof format, validate it against Purifiers ([Helios](https://github.com/a16z/helios), [Nimbus](https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth1/tree/master/nimbus_verified_proxy)); iterate until efficient
    - (c) Kurtosis config to get the root hashes to match, thorough testing with reorgs and pathologic scenarios
    - (d) Decide on storing root hash in block header vs [zk-based alternative](https://notes.ethereum.org/@vbuterin/parallel_post_state_roots), and implement the sync.

### [EIP-7668: Remove bloom filters](https://forkcast.org/upgrade/glamsterdam#eip-7668)

- Backwards-compatible alternative: Only drop the computation, replace with all-1's value (100% false positive).
- [EIP-6466](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6466) also drops logsBloom, but further enables proofs of partial data (reducing L2 complexity), and avoids repeated breakage for dApp buidlers / L2s.
- Parts could be:
    - (a) EIP-6466 receipts to drop receipt bloom field
    - (b) Replace the block header logsBloom with all-1's (backwards compatible)
    - (c) Future: Drop block header logsBloom [when going full SSZ](https://vitalik.eth.limo/general/2024/10/26/futures5.html), or replace with EIP-7745 logIndexRoot.

was talking with Ansgar  about the best way to approach and i think we should do the following for the glam scoping segment of thursday's call:
* each client team has an opportunity to present a high-level (< 1 min) overview of any EIPs they strongly support
* we go through all EL EIPs and try to gain consensus on a DFI candidate list (and after doing this and previous point we may also get some sense of a CFI candidate list)

this should give everyone more info to make a 2nd pass to refine their team's selections for the next ACDE where we can continue the conversation

> Erigon's team view on Glamsterdam: https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/wiki/Glamsterdam-PFI-stand

It states EIP-7610 is implemented already, but note that this is not yet part of the protocol and this EIP is intended to be shipped in to make this part of the protocol. As the EIP state, EIP-161 (which we shipped a long time ago) states that only the codeHash/nonce/balance fields should be checked for the contract creation operation, but not the storage. EIP-7610 makes the storage also part of the protocol. It is a somewhat theoretical case, but with enough computing power an address collision could happen, and there are accounts on mainnet which have storage but the other fields empty.

@jochem-brouwer EIP-7610 is already implemented in geth (https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/28912), erigon (https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/14672) and probably all other clients. It's also implemented in execution-spec-tests (https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/pull/636). It's activated retroactively. So it's already part of the protocol rather than a candidate for Glamsterdam
